common_name: Alizes Tall Bearded Iris (Blue-and-White Bicolor Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Alizes is a tall bearded iris bred by Jean Cayeux and introduced in 1991, carrying the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its reliable garden performance, with white standards tinged light blue over deep blue falls fading toward greenish-white. Plant rhizomes high and shallow in a sunny, lean, well-drained bed in late summer so roots establish before frost. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after bloom to maintain vigor and flowering. It pairs well with other tall bearded cultivars in mixed perennial borders for a classic bicolor display.

common_name: Early Light Tall Bearded Iris (Pale Yellow Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Early Light is a tall bearded iris bred by Nora Scopes, registered in 1983 and later awarded the British Dykes Medal in 1989, holding the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for cream blooms flushed lemon with slightly darker falls. Set rhizomes shallowly in full sun with sharp drainage in late summer to early fall, keeping the top surface of each rhizome exposed to prevent rot. Water sparingly once established, since soggy soil around the rhizome is the most common cause of bacterial soft rot. Lift and divide crowded clumps every three to four years to keep bloom quality high.

common_name: Bumblebee Deelite Miniature Tall Bearded Iris (Yellow-and-Maroon Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Bumblebee Deelite, bred by Jack and Glenda Norrick and registered in 1985, is a miniature tall bearded iris holding the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, with yellow standards and maroon falls edged in yellow around an orange beard. Its slender stems bloom between the median and tall bearded iris seasons, and the proportionately small flowers suit the front of the border where full-size tall bearded blooms would look oversized. Plant rhizomes shallowly in full sun and well-drained soil in late summer, and divide every three to four years once clumps become crowded. The strong yellow-and-maroon pattern also makes it a popular parent in miniature tall bearded breeding programs.

common_name: Langport Wren Intermediate Bearded Iris (Maroon Self Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Langport Wren is an intermediate bearded iris bred by Kelways and introduced in 1973, part of their English 'Langport' series alongside siblings such as 'Langport Claret' and 'Langport Flame', blooming in the gap between the dwarf and tall bearded iris seasons with reddish-purple standards over deep maroon falls. It holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its dependable repeat performance in British garden trials. Grow it in full sun with sharply drained, neutral to slightly alkaline soil, setting rhizomes shallowly in late summer. Its compact habit and rich color suit rock gardens and the front of mixed perennial beds.

common_name: Maui Moonlight Intermediate Bearded Iris (Pale Yellow Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Maui Moonlight, bred by J. Terry Aitken and registered in 1986, is an intermediate bearded iris bearing the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, with softly ruffled, pale lemon-yellow self blooms carried on branched stems midway in height between dwarf and tall bearded types. It blooms in the intermediate season, bridging the gap between early dwarf iris and later tall bearded iris displays. Plant rhizomes shallowly in full sun with excellent drainage, and avoid heavy mulch against the crown to prevent rot. Divide every three to four years to keep flowering vigorous.

common_name: Orinoco Flow Border Bearded Iris (White-and-Violet Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Orinoco Flow, bred by Cy Bartlett and registered in 1993, is a border bearded iris that also earned the British Dykes Medal in 1994 and carries the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit. Its ruffled blooms combine white standards with violet-purple stitching on the falls, a class that produces tall-bearded-type flowers on shorter, more proportionate stems. Plant rhizomes shallowly in full sun and sharply drained soil in late summer, giving plants room to clump before winter dormancy. The compact stature suits mid-border placement where full-size tall bearded iris would overwhelm smaller companions.

common_name: Raspberry Blush Intermediate Bearded Iris (Pink Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Raspberry Blush, bred by Melba Hamblen and registered in 1975, is an intermediate bearded iris holding the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit, with ruffled flowers in raspberry-pink tones deepening toward the beard. Blooming between the dwarf and tall bearded iris seasons, it extends the iris display in beds that also grow earlier and later bearded types. Set rhizomes shallowly in full sun with lean, fast-draining soil in late summer so roots establish before cold weather. Divide congested clumps every three to four years after flowering to sustain bloom performance.

common_name: Sarah Taylor Standard Dwarf Bearded Iris (Cream and Primrose Iris)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes shallowly with tops exposed in late summer to early fall in full sun and sharply drained soil.

directions: Sarah Taylor, bred by John D. Taylor and registered in 1979, is a standard dwarf bearded iris with cream standards and pale primrose falls above a blue beard, blooming well ahead of the tall bearded iris season on short stems. Its diminutive size suits rock gardens, raised beds, and the front edge of borders where larger bearded iris would crowd it out. Plant rhizomes shallowly in full sun with sharp drainage, since dwarf types are especially prone to rot in damp or heavy soil. Divide every two to three years as clumps multiply to keep the planting floriferous.
